title: Advantages, Limitations, and Alternatives knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Advantages, Limitations, and Alternatives?
options: Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
GitHub-hosted runners reduce machine maintenance, while self-hosted runners add control but require stronger isolation, patching, access controls, and cost monitoring.
questions.answer_key: GitHub-hosted runners reduce machine maintenance, while self-hosted runners add control but require stronger isolation, patching, access controls, and cost monitoring.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of advantages, limitations, and alternatives: GitHub-hosted runners reduce machine maintenance, while self-hosted runners add control but require stronger isolation, patching, access controls, and cost monitoring. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Benefits and trade-offs of workflow automation”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
questions.answer_key: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.
questions.explanation: Benefits and trade-offs of workflow automation: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to advantages, limitations, and alternatives?
options: Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: GitHub-hosted runners reduce machine maintenance, while self-hosted runners add control but require stronger isolation, patching, access controls, and cost monitoring. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
